If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (8–14 days), apply a downward correction of 1–2% to the forecast path starting at day 8.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for mid-horizon (8–14 days) to dampen momentum.

If sentiment is mixed and forecast is trending downward, increase slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for mid-horizon (8–14 days) to prevent premature bottoming.

If sentiment is positive at end of horizon (15–30 days) but true price is rising, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to the final 3–5 days to capture late-stage momentum.
